verdict.rationale: Elicit's docs show the Research Agent running core product operations from plain-language instructions. You can add extraction columns by telling the agent, apply filters by stating them in a query, and search with natural-language questions. You can also filter and export sources, save papers to the Library, generate figures and draft slides without leaving the conversation, with reusable skills invoked via /. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration that agent-driven operations (columns, filters, exports) work reliably via natural language, and documentation of which UI actions cannot be done through chat.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: To add a column, simply tell the research agent what column(s) you'd like to add. For example, you can say: "Add a column for study type."
The simplest way to filter is to just say what you want in your Research Agent query. Elicit will automatically detect and apply the right filter.
filter and export your sources, save papers to your Library, generate figures, and draft slides, all without leaving the conversation
you can ask a question in natural language, and Elicit will find relevant papers, without you having to think of every possible keyword to search for.
A skill is a set of instructions you can hand to Elicit's agent so it approaches a task a particular way.
